messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit provisions with the following wording.

1. **Purpose and access.** The testing house may use the drawings and CAD geometry solely to prepare for, perform and report on the agreed actuator vibration tests. Access is limited to test personnel listed by name in a schedule approved in writing by the design owner. Before receiving access, each person must be bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. The testing house is responsible for their compliance. Advisers and subcontractors may receive access only through the same approval process.

2. **Working copies and fixtures.** The testing house may make the minimum working copies, fixture files and physical fixtures reasonably needed for the tests. It must encrypt digital copies and fixture files in transit and at rest, limit access to the named personnel and keep physical fixtures secure. It may use only the geometry needed to locate, mount and test the actuator. Neither the testing house nor anyone receiving access may reuse the drawings, geometry, fixture files or fixtures for another project or use them to develop a competing product.

3. **Destruction and verification.** Within 30 days after the design owner accepts the final test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the work, the testing house must securely erase the drawings, CAD geometry and derived files in its possession or control and destroy the physical fixtures. Within the same period, it must provide a written certificate identifying the materials destroyed, the destruction dates and the verification method. We would accept certification by a mutually agreed independent verifier in place of design-owner site access.

The testing house may retain a final report containing measurements, test conditions and conclusions, provided it excludes drawings and reconstructable CAD geometry. Can you work with that reporting boundary and the 30-day deadline? If an accreditation or backup requirement calls for longer retention, please identify the specific record, required period and access controls so we can agree a narrow exception.

Here is where we land on each provision, with proposed wording.

**1. Reporting boundary — acceptable.** We can work within a final report limited to measurements, test conditions and conclusions, excluding drawings and reconstructable CAD geometry. Suggested tightening:

> "The retained final report may include test data, test conditions and conclusions, but must exclude the drawings, CAD geometry, fixture files and any measurements from which the actuator geometry could be reconstructed."

**2. Thirty-day deadline — acceptable, with two narrow retention exceptions.**

*Calibration records.* Our accredited laboratory's accreditation requires retention of calibration records for 24 months. These records contain equipment identifiers, calibration dates and certificates only — no drawings, geometry or fixture data. Proposed exception:

> "Notwithstanding the above, the testing house may retain equipment calibration records for 24 months from the date of test, provided such records contain no drawings, CAD geometry, fixture files or data from which geometry could be reconstructed. Such records must be limited to the approved personnel, encrypted at rest, identified in the deletion certificate as retained records, and securely destroyed at the end of the retention period."

*Backup rotation.* Encrypted system backups cannot be selectively erased within one rotation cycle:

> "Where the testing house's standard backup rotation exceeds 30 days, encrypted backups containing the materials may persist only until overwritten in the ordinary course, and in any event no more than 90 days after the deletion deadline, subject to the same access controls, with the rotation interval stated in the certificate."

**3. Personnel schedule — needs a substitution mechanism.** Prior written approval of every named individual will stall the job. Our machining subcontractor and laboratory assign personnel per fixture and per test slot, and assignments change mid-job through no fault of ours. Two options:

*Option A (our preference) — substitution on notice:*

> "The testing house may add or substitute personnel of equivalent role by written notice to the design owner. A substitution takes effect on notice unless the design owner objects in writing within five business days on reasonable grounds relating to confidentiality or protection of the drawings. The design owner may require the immediate removal of any individual from access on reasonable grounds, and the testing house remains responsible for that individual's compliance."

*Option B (fallback) — entity-level approval:*

> "Access may be granted to individuals listed by name, or to all personnel of a named organization and role (for example, fixture-machining or test personnel of the named subcontractor), where each individual is bound by written confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement."

Tradeoff: under Option A you keep a short objection window and an unconditional removal right; we keep continuity. Under Option B you approve organizations once; we keep staffing flexibility. Either way we accept responsibility for compliance.

Related practical point: requiring an agreement-specific signed undertaking from every shop-floor technician is not workable. We propose that for subcontractor and laboratory personnel the required undertaking may be our standard written confidentiality obligations plus a project-specific written flow-down notice, which we attest are at least as protective of the drawings as this agreement, with the testing house remaining responsible for their compliance.

**4. Verification — officer certificate as default; no unannounced or third-party site access.** Our machining shop and laboratory are third-party facilities we do not control, and we cannot commit them to inspections. Proposed wording:

> "Verification is by a written certificate signed by an officer of the testing house, identifying the materials destroyed, the destruction dates, the verification method, and any records retained under an agreed exception."

If you require assurance beyond the certificate, we offer, in descending order of preference: (i) supporting evidence delivered with the certificate (destruction logs, IT attestation, photographs of destroyed fixtures); (ii) verification by a mutually agreed independent verifier at your cost; (iii) a single on-site visit at your cost, on at least ten business days' prior written notice, during business hours, escorted, and subject to the site operator's rules. We cannot agree to unannounced inspections or to access at shared third-party sites without the operator's consent.

**5. Working copies and fixtures — acceptable, with one clarification.** Minimum working copies, encryption, named-personnel access, and the no-reuse / no-competing-product restrictions all work. Confirm that fixture files issued to our machining subcontractor fall within "geometry needed to locate, mount and test," since manufacture of mounting fixtures is exactly that use:

> "Fixture files derived from the drawings may be provided to the testing house's approved machining subcontractor solely for manufacture of the physical fixtures for the agreed tests."

**6. Clock certainty.** To make the 30-day period workable, propose that the final report is deemed accepted if you raise no written objection within 15 business days of delivery. You get faster closure; we get a fixed start to the deletion clock.

Open items for your confirmation: (a) Option A or B for substitution; (b) the two retention exceptions as drafted; (c) the verification tier; (d) deemed acceptance. We can close all four quickly if the substitution mechanism lands.

We accept Option A with access effective on notice for named personnel in approved roles and organizations. We also accept the 24-month calibration period, the backup cap of 90 days after the deletion deadline, and deemed acceptance for purposes of starting the deletion clock. We propose the following wording to close the remaining points.

1. **Personnel.** “The parties will agree in writing on an initial schedule of names, roles and organizations. The testing house may add or substitute an individual in an approved role at an approved organization by giving the design owner written notice of the individual’s name, role and organization before granting access. Access may begin on receipt of notice. The design owner may object within five business days and may require removal at any time on reasonable confidentiality or drawing-protection grounds. The testing house must revoke access immediately upon objection, removal or reassignment away from the work.” Standard written obligations plus a project-specific written notice are acceptable if, together, they bind each individual to equivalent confidentiality **and use** restrictions before access. The testing house must attest to that coverage and remains responsible for compliance.

2. **Report and retention.** We accept your retained-report and calibration-record wording as drafted. We also accept your backup wording with this addition. “Backup copies may be accessed solely for disaster recovery. If a backup is restored, the testing house must immediately reapply the required deletions before releasing the restored system for ordinary use. The testing house must confirm in writing when the last affected backup has expired and when the retained calibration records have been destroyed.”

3. **Verification.** We accept your officer-certificate wording with supporting evidence as the default. “The certificate must cover materials held by the testing house and its subcontractors and include deletion logs or IT attestations for digital materials and a destruction record or photograph for each physical fixture. If the evidence leaves a specific discrepancy unresolved after the testing house has had an opportunity to address it, the design owner may obtain a records review by a mutually agreed independent verifier at the design owner’s cost.” This resolves verification without a site visit.

4. **Machining.** We accept your proposed sentence authorizing fixture files for manufacture. Files supplied to the approved machining subcontractor must contain only the geometry needed to make the mounting fixtures. The named-personnel, encryption, destruction and no-reuse provisions apply to those files and the resulting fixtures as applicable, including the prohibition on use to develop competing products.

5. **Deletion clock.** “For purposes of the 30-day destruction period, the final report is accepted on written acceptance or, if earlier, upon expiry of 15 business days after delivery without a written objection identifying a deficiency against the agreed test requirements. Following a timely objection, the same review period applies on delivery of the corrected report. Earlier termination starts the 30-day destruction period on the termination date.” This gives both parties a definite trigger while preserving review of a timely reported deficiency.

Agreed on the package. Two clarifications before we close, both on verification and subcontractor coverage.

**Clarification 1 — scope of the records review.** A records review is acceptable as the final verification step, but it must remain a paper exercise. Proposed wording:

> "Any records review is limited to written and electronic records relevant to deletion, backup expiry and fixture destruction. It does not include any right of on-site access, and the verifier's report to the design owner must be limited to whether the required deletions occurred, without disclosing other confidential information of the testing house, its subcontractors or other customers."

This keeps the verification tier records-only, consistent with our inability to commit third-party facilities to inspection, and confines the verifier's disclosure to the compliance question you need answered.

**Clarification 2 — certificate coverage for subcontractors.** We can cover subcontractor-held materials in the certificate, since the schedule flows the same obligations down. Proposed wording:

> "The certificate covers materials held by the testing house and its subcontractors, based on deletion and destruction records provided to the testing house by those subcontractors. The testing house attests that it has obtained those records and remains responsible for its subcontractors' compliance."

**Everything else confirmed as drafted:**

- Personnel: initial schedule, substitution on notice before access, five-day objection window, immediate revocation on objection, removal or reassignment; standard obligations plus project notice attested as equivalent on confidentiality and use.
- Retention: report without geometry; 24-month calibration records; backups capped at 90 days past the deadline, disaster-recovery access only, re-deletion before restored systems return to ordinary use, written confirmation of last backup expiry and calibration-record destruction.
- Machining: fixture files to the approved machining subcontractor limited to mounting geometry, with named-personnel, encryption, destruction and no-reuse restrictions flowing through.
- Deletion clock: acceptance on written acceptance or 15 business days after delivery without a deficiency objection, same cycle on corrected reports, termination date trigger.

If those two clarifications work for you, we have a closed set of terms and can move to documenting the schedule of approved names, roles and organizations. Confirm and we will send the draft schedule for the machining shop and laboratory personnel within two business days.

We accept both clarifications as drafted. Any independent review will be limited to the specified records, and the verifier’s report will be confined to the compliance finding. The testing house’s officer certificate will cover subcontractor-held materials and attest that the testing house obtained the supporting records. The testing house remains responsible for subcontractor compliance.

The terms are agreed. Please send the draft schedule of names, roles and organizations for the machining shop and laboratory personnel within two business days. Access may begin once both parties approve the initial schedule in writing and the required confidentiality and use restrictions bind each person receiving access.

Below is the draft schedule for approval of structure and scope. We are collecting individual names internally and will circulate the completed schedule with names inserted within two business days. Please confirm the role and organization entries now so that approval of the final names is the only outstanding step.

**Draft Schedule 1 — Approved Personnel, Roles and Organizations**
Project: actuator vibration tests
Effective: on written approval by both parties

| # | Name | Role | Organization | Access scope | Restrictions |
|---|------|------|--------------|--------------|--------------|
| 1 | [to be inserted] | Test lead | Testing house | Drawings, CAD geometry, fixture files, test setup | Standard confidentiality + project-specific use notice |
| 2 | [to be inserted] | Test engineer (x2) | Testing house | Drawings, CAD geometry, fixture files, test execution and reporting | Same |
| 3 | [to be inserted] | Laboratory technician | Accredited laboratory (subcontractor) | Drawings limited to mounting geometry; test conditions | Same, flowed down via testing house |
| 4 | [to be inserted] | Fixture machinist (x2) | Specialist machining shop (subcontractor) | Fixture files limited to mounting geometry only | Same, flowed down via testing house |
| 5 | [to be inserted] | Quality / compliance officer | Testing house | Records only — no geometry; deletion, backup and calibration records | Same |

**Proposed conditions to accompany approval:**

1. Access for each listed individual begins only after that individual is bound by the testing house's standard written confidentiality obligations plus the project-specific written use-restriction notice, which together bind them to confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective of the drawings and geometry as the agreement. The testing house attests to that coverage in writing and remains responsible for compliance.

2. The testing house may add or substitute an individual in a listed role at a listed organization by written notice of name, role and organization before granting access, with access effective on receipt of notice subject to the design owner's five-business-day objection right and removal rights as agreed.

3. Access is revoked immediately on objection, removal, or reassignment away from the work.

4. Fixture files supplied to the machining shop are limited to mounting geometry, with encryption, named-personnel access, destruction and no-reuse restrictions flowing through.

Please confirm items 1–4 and the role/organization scope above, and we will send the completed schedule with names for countersignature within the two-business-day window.

We approve conditions 1–4 and the proposed role, organization and access assignments. The test lead and two test engineers may access drawings, CAD geometry and fixture files as needed for their assigned work. The laboratory technician may receive mounting geometry and test conditions. The two machinists may receive only fixture files limited to mounting geometry. The quality/compliance officer may access deletion, backup and calibration records that exclude geometry.

Please send the completed schedule within two business days, with one row for each of the seven individuals. Identify the accredited laboratory and machining shop by their legal names so that future substitution notices can be matched to the approved organizations.

Access may begin once both parties approve the completed schedule in writing and the testing house has provided the written attestation required by condition 1 for each person receiving access.

Scope assignments approved as stated. We will circulate the completed schedule within two business days as a single table with one row per individual — seven rows covering the test lead, two test engineers, the laboratory technician, the two machinists and the quality/compliance officer — identifying the accredited laboratory and the machining shop by their full legal names so that substitution notices can be matched to the approved organizations.

The completed schedule will be accompanied by the written attestation required under condition 1 for each person receiving access, confirming that the standard written confidentiality obligations plus the project-specific use-restriction notice together bind that individual to confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as the agreement, and that the testing house remains responsible for compliance.

Access will begin only once both parties have approved the completed schedule in writing and those attestations have been provided, and each individual's access will be limited to the approved scope in the schedule. Subsequent substitutions will follow the agreed notice, objection and immediate-revocation procedure.
